events.headline: SynthID detector checks partner watermarks
events.text: Google’s new SynthID website can check for invisible AI watermarks in images, video and audio. Ars Technica reports the detector supports watermarks from OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao, with Apple support coming soon. Google says Gemini has integrated SynthID with more than 180 billion images and videos, plus 240,000 years of audio.

events.headline: Finland halts work at two Google data centres
events.text: Finnish authorities have ordered a halt to building work at two planned Google data centres in Muhos and Kajaani. The BBC reports the order follows concerns about clearing more than 300 hectares of forest. At one site, work was carried out without a mandatory environmental impact assessment. Google said it fell short of its own standards and would follow the agency’s guidance.

events.headline: ChatGPT is getting college planning tools
events.text: OpenAI is bringing college application planning tools to ChatGPT for Teens. The Verge reports the feature will bring application requirements, deadlines, tasks and financial-aid steps into one plan. In the US, it will first focus on students in grades 10 through 12 planning for four-year colleges. The announcement followed a report calling ChatGPT for Teens an “unacceptable risk.”

events.headline: Mistral releases open-weight AI model
events.text: French company Mistral says its new 1 trillion-parameter model can rival leading closed models while remaining open-weight. Ars Technica reports the model is available in preview and is optimized for coding, cyberdefense and specialist fields. A final version is expected by the end of the month. Businesses can run open-weight models at the cost of the computing they use.

events.headline: Healthleap raises $38 million for hospital AI
events.text: Healthleap has raised $38 million to build an AI platform that reads patient records to identify patients at risk of undiagnosed illnesses. TechCrunch reports the platform is deployed in more than 50 hospitals, screening for conditions including malnutrition and delirium. The company has also built programs to identify aspiration pneumonia, pressure ulcers and risk of readmission for congestive heart failure.

events.headline: Webb studies collisions around young stars
events.text: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope is giving astronomers a glimpse of violent collisions that may have shaped our solar system. ScienceDaily reports researchers studied 21 rare extreme debris disks around young stars; their dust can reveal the scale and intensity of planetary collisions.

events.headline: Scientists find way to regrow knee cartilage
events.text: A treatment that blocked the protein 15-PGDH restored naturally lost knee cartilage in old mice. ScienceDaily reports it also helped prevent osteoarthritis after knee injuries similar to ACL tears. Human cartilage samples from knee replacement patients began producing new, functional cartilage after exposure. Researchers say the approach could potentially lead to treatments that regenerate cartilage and reduce the need for knee or hip replacement surgery.

events.headline: Arctic sea ice reaches its 2026 minimum
events.text: Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on September 12, covering an estimated 4.6 million square kilometres. NASA reports that ice covered less of the Arctic Ocean at its annual maximum and minimum than it did a few decades ago. Each of the past 20 summers ranks among the 20 lowest minimum extents in the satellite record.

events.text: Three women have been falsely identified and harassed in connection with a Cornell student’s lawsuit, and the plaintiff has received threats too. Her identity is known to her lawyers, the judge and the people she accuses.

events.headline: Little safety data for gray-market peptides
events.text: There is little to no safety data for many gray-market peptides, and concrete evidence is difficult to find. The Verge reports BPC-157 is not approved by any regulatory body and has limited human clinical evidence. A 2025 review found 35 preclinical studies and a single clinical study in humans. The article says BPC-157 videos drew more than 50 million views on YouTube and TikTok in 2024.

events.headline: Curiosity rover captures Martian dawn panorama
events.text: And finally: NASA’s Curiosity rover captured a panorama of wind-carved Martian cliffs at 8:30 a.m. local Mars time. NASA says six images were stitched together, with blue hues preserved in the foreground. The scene features yardangs on Mount Sharp, where Curiosity has reached 0.6 miles in elevation.
